title: Yakitori
subtitle: Japanese grilled chicken skewers with tare sauce
excerpt: Yakitori are Japanese grilled chicken skewers brushed with a sweet-salty tare sauce of soy, honey, and mirin. Thread chicken thigh and spring onion onto skewers and cook in a hot pan or griddle. Simple, quick, and deeply savoury.
sourceNotes: Yakitori means grilled chicken in Japanese. It refers to skewered chicken pieces grilled over charcoal. Yakitori stalls became common in Japan in the Meiji era (1868--1912) as chicken became more widely eaten. Today, dedicated yakitori restaurants and casual street stalls are found throughout Japan.

content.text: The tare sauce is the heart of yakitori. It is a simple reduction of soy sauce, mirin, and honey that becomes glossy and slightly sticky as it cooks. Apply it only at the end -- it will scorch if it goes on too early. Chicken thigh is the best cut for skewers because it stays moist over high heat.
Mix the soy sauce, honey, and mirin in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until slightly thickened. This is the tare sauce.
Thread the chicken chunks and spring onion lengths alternately onto skewers (soak wooden skewers in water first).
Brush the skewers with a little oil. Grill in a hot griddle pan or frying pan over high heat for 4 to 5 minutes per side.
Brush the tare sauce over the skewers during the last 2 minutes of cooking. The sauce will caramelise.
Serve with extra tare sauce on the side and steamed rice.

items.symptom: Sauce burns before the chicken is cooked through
items.cause: Heat too high or sauce applied too early
items.fix: Apply the tare sauce only in the final 2 minutes of cooking. Keep the heat at medium-high rather than maximum to avoid scorching.

content.text: Yakitori shops in Japan are simple, smoky places. They serve skewers over charcoal with cold beer. Every part of the chicken is used -- thighs, skin, livers, hearts. The sweet-salty tare sauce is the signature. Home cooks use a griddle pan or grill to good effect.
